headline: Committees finalized recommendations for the October Special Town Meeting while elementary school planners advanced a $38 million Neary addition and renovation plan.
synopsis: Ahead of the October 17 Special Town Meeting, town boards reviewed and staked out positions on warrant articles covering zoning, capital projects, and municipal finance. The Advisory Committee recommended approval for establishing a stormwater enterprise fund and spending $240,000 from water reserves to connect two homes near the Parkerville Road landfill to town water, but opposed Community Preservation Act funding for both a Peninsula Trail footbridge and Southborough Golf Club irrigation. The Zoning Board of Appeals endorsed a zoning amendment permitting two-family dwellings by special permit, which Advisory recommended against over density and septic concerns. Meanwhile, the Elementary School Building Committee moved toward a $38 million addition and renovation for Neary Elementary after analysis showed a $15 million limited upgrade would be consumed almost entirely by code mandates. Consultants also delivered initial findings to the Select Board regarding Southborough's overall governance and committee structure.

top_items.title: Neary School Building Committee backs $38 million addition-renovation
top_items.why: Architectural analysis revealed that a $15 million upgrade option yields only $5.8 million in direct repairs after mandatory building code upgrades, leaving boilers, ventilation, and classrooms unaddressed.
top_items.body: Tappé Architects presented a cost breakdown showing that required code upgrades, including full fire sprinklers and accessibility compliance, would consume most direct construction funds in a $15 million limited upgrade. That option would leave no funding for replacing aging boilers or unit ventilators and would not qualify for state reimbursement. The Elementary School Building Committee concluded the limited scope is non-viable and directed architects to prepare schematic designs for a $38 million addition and renovation plan ahead of a formal vote.

top_items.title: Town boards split on Peninsula Trail footbridge CPA funding
top_items.why: The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to send a $217,318 supplemental funding request to Town Meeting, despite unanimous opposition from the Advisory Committee over project costs.
top_items.body: Article 4 requests $217,318 in additional Community Preservation Act funds to construct a 65-foot prefabricated pedestrian footbridge along Route 30, bringing the total project cost to $428,550. The Advisory Committee voted against the appropriation due to an estimated bridge cost of roughly $5,000 per linear foot, and the Select Board also voted against it. After considering a floor amendment to cut contingency funds, the Trails Committee and CPC decided to present the funding request to Special Town Meeting as originally drafted.

top_items.title: Dispute over funding golf course irrigation with CPA money
top_items.why: Town officials head into Special Town Meeting divided over whether to allocate over $433,000 in new Community Preservation Act funds toward a $1.09 million golf course irrigation system.
top_items.body: Article 3 asks voters to extend $550,000 in previously approved CPA funds, authorize $433,546 in new CPA funds, and draw $100,000 from the Golf Course Revolving Fund to replace the Southborough Golf Club irrigation system. The Golf Committee and Community Preservation Committee support the article, while the Advisory Committee opposes using tax-supported CPA revenues for a facility intended to be financially self-sustaining. The Golf Committee voted to approve flyer expenses and confirmed it will present the article without amendments.

top_items.title: Two-family dwelling zoning amendment advances to Town Meeting
top_items.why: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted to support Article 2 as drafted, while the Advisory Committee issued an unfavorable recommendation citing septic and density impacts.
top_items.body: Article 2 would eliminate the two-year ownership waiting period to convert existing single-family homes into two-family dwellings and allow new two-family construction by special permit. The Zoning Board of Appeals debated potential impacts on undersized lots before voting unanimously to back the warrant article language as written. The Advisory Committee recommended against approval, expressing concern about speculative purchases, lot sizes in Residential B districts, and septic capacity.

top_items.title: Advisory recommends $240,000 water extension near landfill
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee voted 6-0 to recommend connecting two homes near the Parkerville Road landfill to municipal water to eliminate contamination risks.
top_items.body: Article 7 on the Special Town Meeting warrant requests $240,000 from water retained earnings to extend a municipal water main to two residences near the inactive Parkerville Road landfill. Following clarification that the town will cover the installation of service lines from the street into the houses, the Advisory Committee unanimously endorsed the article to address private well contamination concerns.

top_items.title: Consultant presents initial municipal governance structure study
top_items.why: A preliminary review compared Southborough's governance model and town manager authority against other Massachusetts communities.
top_items.body: Bill Keegan of Capital Strategic Strategies presented an initial progress update to the Select Board on the town government structure study. The 18-week study is analyzing town manager executive powers, committee structures across the town's numerous boards, and potential transitions between charter and bylaw frameworks. The Select Board accepted the update as part of the ongoing review.
